Then which of the following statements is correct (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, above the x-axis there exists a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward, with magnetic induction intensity B. In the xOy plane, from the origin O, a positively charged particle is emitted at a speed v along a direction making an angle θ (0<θ<π) with the positive direction of the x-axis (gravity neglected). When the emission speed v is fixed, how does the motion time of the particle in the magnetic field change with θ?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When v is fixed, the larger θ is, the shorter the time the particle moves in the magnetic field is.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, O is taken as the origin, the horizontal direction to the right is the positive direction of the x-axis, and the vertical direction upward is the positive direction of the y-axis; many “×” symbols are distributed above the x-axis, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward; the particle is emitted from point O, the initial velocity direction is within the range of the first and second quadrants, making an angle θ with the +x-axis, and the arrow in the figure is drawn above the x-axis. Then reason: A positively charged particle moves in a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward. From the direction of the Lorentz force, it can be known that the force is always perpendicular to the velocity and makes the velocity direction rotate counterclockwise, so the trajectory is a circular arc. When the speed v is fixed, the radius of circular motion R=mv/(qB), and the angular velocity ω=qB/m, both have nothing to do with θ. The particle enters the magnetic field above the x-axis from O, and leaves the magnetic field when it intersects the x-axis again. From the fact that the center of the circle is on the left side of the line passing through O and perpendicular to the initial velocity, and from the geometric relationship of the circle, it can be obtained that the central angle traversed by the particle in the magnetic field is 2π-2θ. Therefore the motion time t=(2π-2θ)/ω=2(π-θ)m/(qB). Since ω is constant, t decreases as θ increases.
